newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen A, B shares end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A, B shares end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index inched lower on Wednesday on profit-taking after the index had risen for four straight sessions and the A share index also closed lower on profit-taking, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.13 points, or 0.15 percent, to 91.17 on turnover of HK$19.62 million, compared with HK$18.21 million on Tuesday.

The A share index tumbled 7.07 points, or 1.81 percent, to end at 383.96, with turnover falling to 11.74 billion yuan from 16.40 billion. The composite index dropped 6.33 points, or 1.74 percent, to 357.56.
The B index was hurt by Shenbao, which fell HK$0.40, or 14.81 percent, to HK$2.30 on volume of 39,980 shares. It surged nearly 30 percent on Tuesday on speculative buying.
Profit-taking was mainly targeted at Shenzhen-based counters, which were among Tuesday's top gainers, brokers said.
On the B share market, Victor Onward, the second worst performer, sank HK$0.17, or 9.55 percent, to HK$1.61 on light volume of 7,484 shares on speculative selling, brokers said.
Fangda, which had seen steady advances over the past few sessions, slipped HK$0.06 to HK$5.99 on the session's second most active trade of 671,000 shares.
Dadonghai followed suit, shedding HK$0.02 to HK$1.35, with 622,200 shares changing hands.

Property issue Hainan Pearl River was the star on speculative buying, brokers said. It gained HK$0.12, or 6.15 percent, to HK$2.07. Diesel engine maker Changchai, aided by institutional demand, rose HK$0.02 to HK$5.00 in active trade of 871,300 shares.
On the A share market, wool blanket maker Guangdong Meiya was the focus of profit-taking, brokers said. The counter plunged 0.91 yuan, or 6.91 percent, to 12.25 yuan.
Brokers said they expect the A share market to enter a period of correction after the A share index soared more thnn 200 percent since April this year.
Newcomer Mudanjiang Petrochemical fell 0.91 yuan, or 6.57 percent, to 12.95 yuan.
Chemical fibre maker Kunshan Sanshan bucked the trend with a surge of 2.17 yuan, or 27.54 percent, to 10.05 yuan. Brokers gave no reason for the counter's strong performance.
